title: Shark Attacks
text:
The Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) is a long-running record of reported shark-human incidents around the world. It offers a way to explore where and when these events have been recorded, while keeping individual incidents in a broader context.
Fear of sharks is understandable, but dramatic stories can make attacks seem far more common than they are. In reality, shark attacks are rare, and fatal attacks rarer still; recorded incidents should not be confused with the everyday risk of going in the water.
Explore the Map to see recorded attack counts by country, or visit Trends to see how annual counts change over time. These pages show patterns in the records, not a prediction of the risk to any one person.
